$comment: The mutation floor, per declared scope. Spec: docs/spec/the-ratchet.md.
This file is beside stryker.config.mjs on purpose: `configHash` below ties the two
together, and a diff that changes the timeout and re-derives the floors should show
both changes in the same directory.
EVERY SCOPE IS `unarmed`, AND NOTHING HERE REFUSES ANYTHING YET. A floor is derived
from observed history — the lowest score a scope reached across 20 consecutive healthy
CI runs with no gap over 3 days — and applied ONCE, BY HAND, at arming. Arming is a
human judgement, per scope, after that scope's window fills. There is no moment at
which `the ratchet` becomes armed; every scope is its own decision. `pnpm deploy:site`
prints how far each window has filled at every deploy.
The rule initialises; it does not maintain. After arming, a floor moves UP by hand and
never down on its own — re-deriving is lowering, and costs a justification like any
other lowering.
`floor`   a number this scope may not score under, or `unarmed`.
`armed`   the date the entry was added, or the date it was armed. It is what makes
`unarmed for 94 days` printable, and it is the only guard on somebody
typing `unarmed` to make a refusal go away.
`ignored` disable directives in this scope's mutated source. Asserted against a real
sweep of the tree by `gates/ignored-mutants.test.ts`, at merge. There are
zero in this repo, so any increase is a real event.
`notes`   APPEND-ONLY, one line per lowering, never cleared. A bare number going 44.1
to 41.0 is a diff that says nothing about why; the justification belongs
next to the permission, permanently, where whoever next opens this file
reads it. Nothing enforces this — the file makes an omission visible, it
does not make it impossible.
`configHash` is the score-affecting Stryker configuration these floors were derived
under. Each CI run stamps its own; deploy compares them, and a mismatch refuses rather
than silently comparing two numbers that do not mean the same thing. Lowering
timeoutMS raises the score with no test touched, because a timeout counts as detected.
See scripts/lib/floors.ts for which options are hashed and which are not.
There is no override flag for any refusal this file produces, and that is the design
rather than an omission. See docs/adr/0061-the-mutation-floor-refuses-deploy.md.
